correctness.rationale: For a fixed SPD matrix, diagonalize once; on mode λ each error is multiplied by 1−B_i h_i λ. Independence across attempts (not across eigenmodes) gives the product of expected squared multipliers, and a pure mode at any admissible λ realizes the robust spectral objective. Write z=λ/m, m=(μ+L)/2, c=(L−μ)/(L+μ), B=1−p+pc². Repeating a normalized step a minimizes the maximum absolute endpoint residual uniquely at a=1. At a_i=1+x_i, independently expanded the weighted endpoint certificate with weights (1+c)/2 and (1−c)/2. After subtracting B² it is p(1−c²) times [1−p(1+c²)](x₁²+x₂²)+2pc²(x₁+x₂+x₁x₂)²+p(1+c²)x₁²x₂². Thus p≤1/(1+c²) suffices globally, and even at equality the last two terms force x₁=x₂=0. For p above that bound, splitting symmetrically by d changes the objective by 2pz²[1−p−p(1−z)²]d²+p²z⁴d⁴, negative uniformly near either endpoint for small d, with uniform strict baseline slack on the compact remaining interval. Take d<1. The minimizing pair exists by continuity and coercivity, including p=1: at least one endpoint has |1−a₂z|≥c independently of a₂, while at both endpoints |1−a₁z| tends uniformly to infinity when a₁ does; exchange the steps for the other case. In the rational example, direct integer coefficient multiplication gives the quartic numerator [62500,−225000,311400,−194400,46656] in ascending powers of z, divided by 62500. Its second-derivative numerator discriminant is −34264166400 with positive leading coefficient. Thus the endpoint values 3233/31250 and 2873/31250 give the exact maximum, below 169/1600. No closed-form optimizer above the transition is proved. The supplied symbolic checker and output were inspected, not executed.

evidence: Sambharya–Stellato optimize the sum over input instances of squared deterministic two-step residuals, using spectral moments. Their Theorem 4 gives two distinct optimal steps under its nondegeneracy assumption.
Agarwal–Goel–Zhang derive the deterministic Chebyshev construction and consider bounded gradient perturbations, not independently omitted updates in a mean-square risk.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Optimizing a fixed instance average or a deterministic Chebyshev residual does not cover the present worst-λ observer and Bernoulli loss model. The fixed-distribution objective can be a lower-bound device for a robust objective, but neither prior treats the two additional one-step risks or proves the sharp equality regime when they are included.

evidence: Spectral normalization gives ∏_i[(1−p)+p(1−a_i z)²], a product of per-attempt expected squares. Agarwal–Goel–Zhang optimize a deterministic residual polynomial ∏_i(1−a_i z).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For p=1 the two objectives have the same minimizing steps after squaring the deterministic norm. For p<1, the random-subset one-step and zero-step terms are additional design-dependent contributions (the zero-step contribution is constant); simply squaring the deterministic polynomial or using the mean iterate is not equivalent.

value.rationale: This gives an exact design boundary for a natural two-attempt budget: independently losing a step can make repetition uniquely optimal even when unequal steps would accelerate at perfect delivery. The lower-regime global certificate and full-interval strict improvement above the threshold distinguish those mechanisms, not just local instability. No conclusion is drawn about adaptive or longer schedules, or an unequal optimizer formula.
